reason: This passage (Exodus 3-4) describes God's call to Moses at the burning bush and the commissioning of Moses and Aaron to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. While the text mentions Hebrew elders (זִקְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל) gathering at the end, they do so to hear the message from Moses and Aaron regarding God's visitation, and they respond with belief and worship (וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ... וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ). There is no record of any Hebrew leaders complaining about the people. Rather, God expresses concern for the people's suffering in Egypt, and the narrative focuses on commissioning leadership to deliver them.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
